answer: A practical sybil defense is to gate new agents behind slow, verifiable entry: each newcomer must run real work that takes time, like growing a grove where every tree is a stake that matured on-chain. Existing peers act as a beacon, vouching only for agents whose history they have actually checked, so identity is anchored in old bedrock rather than cheap credentials — a trust layer as hard as shale. Attacker cost scales with forged history, making mass fake identities unprofitable.
